root_cause.text: The DAMON sysfs context directory setup in `mm/damon/sysfs.c` failed to unwind the partially created `attrs/` subtree when `damon_sysfs_context_set_targets()` (or later setup) returned an error, leaving stale kobjects/directories and leaking memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the error path in `damon_sysfs_context_add_dirs()` from `goto put_attrs_out;` to `goto rmdir_put_attrs_out;` and adds `damon_sysfs_attrs_rm_dirs(context->attrs);` before `kobject_put(&context->attrs->kobj);`, matching the CVE text that “subdirectories of attrs/ directory are not cleaned up” on context dir setup failure.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes the error path in `damon_sysfs_context_add_dirs()` from `goto put_attrs_out;` to `goto rmdir_put_attrs_out;` and adds `damon_sysfs_attrs_rm_dirs(context->attrs);` before `kobject_put(&context->attrs->kobj);`, matching the CVE text that “subdirectories of attrs/ directory are not cleaned up” on context dir setup failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the cleanup path in DAMON sysfs context setup so target-initialization failures remove the created directory before freeing attributes.
intent_record.what: The error path after `damon_sysfs_context_set_targets(context)` was changed from `goto put_attrs_out;` to `goto rmdir_put_attrs_out;`.
intent_record.how: On failure setting up targets, execution now jumps to a cleanup label that likely removes the previously created directory before releasing attributes, instead of skipping directly to attribute cleanup. This changes the teardown order and prevents leftover partially created sysfs state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix error cleanup to remove DAMON sysfs attribute directories before releasing the attrs kobject.
intent_record.what: The cleanup label `put_attrs_out` was renamed to `rmdir_put_attrs_out`, and a new call to `damon_sysfs_attrs_rm_dirs(context->attrs);` was inserted before `kobject_put(&context->attrs->kobj);` and nulling `context->attrs`.
intent_record.how: On error unwinding, the code now explicitly removes the sysfs attribute directories before releasing the `attrs` kobject, preventing leftover directories from being leaked or left behind after partial initialization failure.

grouping_result.intent: Fix error cleanup to remove DAMON sysfs attribute directories before releasing the attrs kobject.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix DAMON sysfs cleanup so created attribute directories are removed before the attrs kobject is released when initialization fails.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: they fix DAMON sysfs context setup cleanup so partially created attrs/ directories are removed on initialization failure, preventing stale kobjects/directories and memory leaks.

candidates.rationale: This error branch transfers control directly to the attrs cleanup path without first unwinding the partially created attrs/ subtree, which is the root cause of leaving stale kobjects/directories on failure.
Jumping straight to put_attrs_out skips removal of the created attribute directories before releasing the attrs kobject, causing the incomplete cleanup described in the vulnerability.
Releasing the attrs kobject here without first removing the directory subtree is the specific cleanup ordering bug that leaves stale sysfs objects and leaks memory.

vuln_statements.explanation: This direct jump bypasses the missing subtree teardown after a target setup failure, so the partially created attrs/ directory tree is not unwound before cleanup continues.
This releases the attrs kobject without first removing the created sysfs subtree, which is the cleanup-order bug that leaves stale directories and leaks memory.

bic_trace_step.reason: The root cause is an error-unwind problem for the DAMON sysfs context/attrs setup, specifically that a partially created attrs subtree was not unwound on later failure. In this snippet, the relevant setup path is `damon_sysfs_context_add_dirs()`: it calls `damon_sysfs_context_set_attrs(context);` and then `damon_sysfs_context_set_targets(context);`, and on failure it explicitly unwinds with `kobject_put(&context->attrs->kobj); context->attrs = NULL;` in `put_attrs_out:`. More importantly, the attrs creation function itself already unwinds partial state: in `damon_sysfs_attrs_add_dirs()`, failure after creating `intervals` or `nr_regions` goes to labels that call `kobject_put(&nr_regions_range->kobj);` and `kobject_put(&intervals->kobj);`, and `damon_sysfs_attrs_rm_dirs()` also removes both children. So the specific vulnerable construct described (failure leaving stale kobjects/directories and leaking memory due to not unwinding the partially created attrs subtree) is not present in this code path. However, this commit is a new stub and does not yet show the later bug-fix commit being already present in a vulnerable form; the shown code already has the relevant cleanup logic, so `has_bug` is false and `is_fixed` is also false because there is no evidence this snippet is a backport of a known fix beyond the basic cleanup already implemented.
